newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to sign deals with foreign oil cos.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to sign deals with foreign oil cos.

text.p: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Tuesday that Bangladesh would award rights for 15 exploration blocks to foreign oil and gas companies by mid-July.

"We have just had most successful licencing bidding for gas and oil exploration in London and Houston," Hasina told foreign and local investors while visiting the Dhaka Export Processing Zone at Savar 25 miles (40 km) from Dhaka.
She said more than than 60 leading oil and gas companies from around the world had participated in the bidding.
"We are expecting to sign production-sharing contracts for the remaining 15 exploration blocks by the 15th of July," she added.
Bangladesh has earmarked 23 exploration blocks on land and offshore for participation by foreign companies.
The country has already offered eight blocks to overseas companies like Cairn Energy Plc, Holland Sea Search, United Meridian Corp and Occidental Corp.
"The extraordinery interest...shown by investors in the energy sector is the result of our liberal and open-door policy on investment," the prime minister said.
Hasina said Bangladesh was offering the "best possible" incentives and facilities to attract investment for faster economic growth.
She said "trade and not foreign aid only should help a nation to prosper. "Our slogan is produce or perish," she said.
Hasina said her government had further liberalised economic policies to raise export, import and investment.
She said the country would set up more exclusive industrial zones for foreign investors as there was encouraging overseas response.
Government officials said on Tuesday that investment on industries reached $240 million by mostly foreign companies in the exclusive industrial zones in Chittagong and Dhaka.
Export from the two zones contributed nine percent to the country's total export earnings of $3.8 billion in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June), they said.

The officials said the companies in the exclusive zones would be allowed tax holiday for 10 years, duty free exports, duty free imports of machinery, equipment and raw materials, and be exempted of income tax on salaries of foreign technicians for three years.
Hasina said: "Investors may also take advantage of the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) which allows duty free or reduced duty access to the markets in America, Europe and Japan."
"Rstrictions on movement of foreign exchange have been totally abolished. Foreigners are allowed to bring in, process and take out foreign currency freely," she said.
